lines.say: Louisiana, around 2000. A two-year-old boy named James Leininger starts having nightmares. Screaming: airplane crash, on fire, can't get out.
shots: q: vintage toy airplane on floor

lines.say: He talks about flying a Corsair, a World War Two fighter, from a ship called the Natoma.
shots: archive: F4U Corsair WWII photo (US Navy, public domain)
archive: USS Natoma Bay escort carrier (public domain)

lines.say: He says he had a friend there named Jack Larsen. And he says the pilot was named James, like him.
His father, a skeptic, starts researching to prove him wrong.
He finds the USS Natoma Bay. A pilot named Jack Larsen served on it. And one pilot from it was killed near Iwo Jima in 1945: James Huston Junior.
shots: archive: Natoma Bay squadron photo (public domain)
line art: name James M. Huston Jr. typed

lines.say: Skeptics point out the family visited an aviation museum before the nightmares, and that details sharpened as the parents researched.
shots: line art: timeline showing museum visit

lines.say: Researchers at the University of Virginia call it one of their strongest American cases. Both readings are still on the table.
